bib.title: WFM: Wiki Foundation Model for Complex Agentic Reasoning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "WFM: Wiki Foundation Model for Complex Agentic Reasoning", Junnan Dong, Linhao Luo, Senlei Zhang et al. (Tencent Youtu Lab, Monash and others). arXiv 2609.18182v1, cs.AI, 16 Sep 2026. It is a preprint. The ACM template is unfilled ("Conference acronym 'XX", "Anonymous Authors"), so it was formatted for a venue but has no venue.

COVERAGE: All 54,646 chars read, from the first page through the references (the last reference is [39]). There are no appendices. Nothing was skimmed. Tables 1-4 and the Figure 3 and 5 numbers came through as text. The figure images were not viewed.

NOTE FIT: Note 12 is a weak fit. WFM is a trained graph foundation model (GAT-style encoder, GPU training) used as a retriever. It is not about shared typed or provenance-carrying memory across agents. The nearest fit is `13-graph-ml-and-gnns` (or `13b-representation-learning-and-gnns`), because the contribution is GNN/GFM representation learning, attention collapse and distributed training. Note 12 could take it as a one-line counterpoint: its memory benchmarks are single-user long-history QA, not multi-agent write paths. Notes 01, 05, 06 and 07 do not fit. `11-kg-rag-and-text-to-cypher` is a secondary option, since the paper compares against GraphRAG.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- A tuned, text-augmented graph retriever beats GraphRAG baselines on multi-hop QA. WFM scores best on all three datasets in both modes.
  number: Open/Reject 89.6/84.3 (HotpotQA), 90.2/82.4 (2Wiki), 69.8/52.6 (MuSiQue). Gains over Youtu-GraphRAG are 2.8/4.1, 3.2/4.8 and 4.1/5.1 points.
  setup: 1,000 held-out questions per dataset. Generator DeepSeek V4 Flash, judge DeepSeek V4 Pro, embeddings all-MiniLM-L6-v2, retrieval depth 20, 3 attention layers, reflection budget B=4. Reject mode means the generator may use only retrieved evidence. Open mode also allows parametric knowledge.
  quote: "WFM achieves the strongest Open and Reject accuracy on all three benchmarks, reaching 89.6/84.3 on HotpotQA, 90.2/82.4 on 2Wiki, and 69.8/52.6 on MuSiQue."
  where: Sec 4.5, Table 2

- Long-horizon memory QA improves over memory-specific systems.
  number: PersonaMem 58.49 and RHELM 52.17 overall, +8.39 and +5.37 over the strongest baseline. Without reflection: 54.12 and 48.90.
  setup: PersonaMem 1M (2,674 questions, 20 personas) and the RHELM 1M, seven-category setting. Baselines are A-mem, MemoryOS, LightMem, Native RAG and GraphRAG variants. Zero-shot full-context is also a baseline.
  quote: "Full WFM reaches 58.49 on PersonaMem and 52.17 on RHELM, exceeding the strongest baseline overall by 8.39 and 5.37 points, respectively."
  where: Sec 4.6, Table 3
  Caution: in Table 3 the RHELM zero-shot full-context baseline scores 46.8 overall. That is above every non-WFM retrieval method there (A-mem 37.8), and WFM w/o reflection (48.90) is only 2.1 points above it. The text's "strongest baseline" delta of 5.37 for the full model implies 46.8 as the comparator. The same table shows Native RAG at 28.7 and GFM-RAG at 6.5 on RHELM.

- Dense passage nodes matter, and plain triples lose to them.
  number: replacing the Wiki Graph with an entity-only graph drops average multi-hop Recall@20 by 7.48 points and memory accuracy by 7.68 points.
  setup: ablation. Averages are Recall@20 over HotpotQA, 2Wiki and MuSiQue, and overall accuracy over PersonaMem and RHELM. Full WFM scores 86.20 and 55.33.
  quote: "replacing the Wiki Graph with an ordinary entity graph causes a 7.48-point drop in average multi-hop recall and a 7.68-point drop in memory accuracy"
  where: Sec 4.7, Fig 5

- Self-reflection (an iterative retrieve-and-answer loop) helps, and an adaptive stop cuts its cost.
  number: memory accuracy goes from 51.51 (one round) to 55.33 (B=4). It reaches only 55.57 at B=6. At B=4 the agent executes 2.58 rounds on average. Forcing all rounds costs 1.58× wall-clock.
  setup: ablation and parameter sweep, same setting as above.
  quote: "at 𝐵 = 4, the agent executes 2.58 rounds on average."
  where: Sec 4.8, Fig 3b and Fig 5

- Attention collapse is the problem the paper targets, and the fix is a variance hinge loss plus a warm start. L_var = Σ[ε − Var(π)]+, with ε=0.05 and λ2=0.1.
  number: removing L_var drops average Recall@20 from 86.20 to 82.47. Removing the warm start drops it to 80.36.
  quote: "Removing variance regularization or warm-starting also consistently hurts both metrics"
  where: Sec 3.4, 4.7, Fig 5
  The paper gives no direct measurement of the collapse itself, only the ablation.

- Systems claim: fixed-shape NCCL boundary exchange cuts step time.
  number: 2.40s to 0.23s per step, 10.5×. The paper calls it "bit-exact".
  setup: the cluster size, GPU count and graph size are not stated in the extracted text.
  quote: "reduces the measured per-step latency from 2.40s to 0.23s, corresponding to a 10.5× end-to-end acceleration while preserving the computed node states."
  where: Sec 3.5

- Depth sweet spot.
  number: 3 layers peak (86.20 average R@20, 55.33 memory accuracy). Deeper stacks degrade.
  quote: "Performance improves through three layers as increasingly distant passages become reachable, peaking at 86.20 average Recall@20 and 55.33 memory accuracy."
  where: Sec 4.8

- Retrieval recall.
  number: Recall@20 is 93.20 (HotpotQA), 90.15 (2Wiki) and 75.24 (MuSiQue). The last is 0.66 below Youtu-GraphRAG's 75.90. On PersonaMem, WFM is 0.24 below A-mem at k=5 (23.46 vs 23.7) and ahead at k=10 and k=20.
  quote: "On MuSiQue, it leads through 𝑘 = 10 and reaches 75.24 at 𝑘 = 20, within 0.66 points of Youtu-GraphRAG."
  where: Sec 4.5, Table 1

LIMITS
- The authors' own caveat, which matters most: "The newly completed cells and diagnostic sweeps are constructed planning values and require validation with measured runs before external use." (Sec 4.4). Every headline number above is therefore at risk, and it is not clear which cells are the "newly completed" ones. Treat all figures as unverified.
- It is one author group, and Youtu-GraphRAG and GFM-RAG are the authors' own prior systems. No code release, seeds, variance or confidence intervals are mentioned.
- The ablation averages and Figure 3 sweeps are tuned on the same memory benchmarks used for reporting. ε and λ2 were picked by best memory accuracy.
- The LLM judge and generator are DeepSeek V4. PersonaMem recall uses an LLM judge, so recall is not comparable across datasets.
- DistMult is run with a capped neighbourhood because the uncapped version goes OOM at 1M. That makes it a weakened baseline.
- It is single-user memory QA only. It has no multi-agent concurrent writes, provenance, false-merge or staleness handling, or governance. The graph is built from a wiki, and wiki construction cost and quality are not evaluated.
- The conclusion's "eliminating GPU memory OOM boundaries" has no separate supporting result in the text.
- "Paradigm shift ... entire industry" is asserted. The only cited basis is Karpathy's llm-wiki gist.
- Future work named: real-time dynamic tasks and generalisation.

BUILDS ON
- Karpathy, llm-wiki gist, 2026 (the LLM Wiki concept).
- GFM-RAG (Luo et al., arXiv 2502.01113, 2025) and G-reasoner (Luo et al., ICLR 2026).
- Youtu-GraphRAG (Dong et al., arXiv 2508.19855, 2025).
- GraphRAG (Edge et al., arXiv 2404.16130, 2024), LightRAG (2024), RAPTOR (Sarthi et al., ICLR 2024).
- HippoRAG (NeurIPS 2024) and HippoRAG2 (Gutiérrez et al., ICML 2025).
- Memory baselines: A-mem (Xu et al., arXiv 2502.12110, 2025), MemoryOS (EMNLP 2025), LightMem (2026).
- Method roots: TransE-style margin loss, InfoNCE, a KGAT-like Bi-Interaction aggregator (not cited by name in the extraction), and ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) for the loop.
- Benchmarks: HotpotQA (2018), 2Wiki (2020), MuSiQue (TACL 2022), PersonaMem (Jiang et al., 2025), RHELM (Zhang et al., 2026).

CODE: none. The load-bearing formulas are:
- Eq 3, relation-aware attention score: π(v,r,u)=w_aᵀ tanh(W_r h_u + e_r − W_r h_v).
- Eq 11, variance hinge: L_var = Σ_v [ε − Var_{u∈N(v)}(π(v,r,u))]+.

FIGURES
- Figure 5 (ablation, effectiveness and relative wall-clock cost), around p.7. It shows in one view which component carries the gain: ordinary graph 78.72, DistMult 74.31, w/o var 82.47, w/o warm start 80.36, w/o self-reflection 81.08 (Recall@20) against full 86.20. It also shows the cost of each variant (DistMult 2.65×, forcing all rounds 1.58×). I did not view the image, so check the caption with `figures.py captions`.
- Figure 1 would be the alternative for the RAG, GraphRAG and LLM-Wiki framing, but it is conceptual only.

PROBLEMS
- The ACM template text is unfilled (placeholder venue, "Anonymous Authors", 2018 dates).
- The extraction scrambles Figure 1 text and the Table 1 MuSiQue R@20 cell ("71.9575.24" is 71.95 and 75.24). Table 4's PersonaMem R@10/R@20 for WFM are fused as "23.46 37.3952.63", which is 23.46, 37.39 and 52.63.
- The paper says the 10.5× speedup is "bit-exact". I did not check this.
- Embedded instructions: none found. The "constructed planning values" sentence is a data-validity warning, not an instruction.
